alt: An emperor's private notebook. What fills the whole first book? A  complaints / B  thank-yous Reply A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
B. A whole book of thank-yous. Before any advice to himself, Marcus Aurelius names the people who shaped him, one by one: a grandfather, his mother, teachers, a brother, friends. Meditations, Book 1.
Meditations, Book 5, line one. What is the emperor writing about? A  war / B  getting out of bed / C  taxes Reply A, B or C. Answer tomorrow at 9.
B. Getting out of bed. “In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present—I am rising to the work of a human being.” Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 5.1, tr. George Long.
More of which next week? A  history / B  mind / C  kindness Reply A, B or C. Most replies wins.
One small thing for the weekend. Send one line to someone who taught you something this year. “From you I learned…” is enough. From Thursday's thank-you list.
Who made your week better? One name. They don't have to know. (They should, though.) Reply with one word.
What's the one thing you're already worried about this week? Just the word. Nobody else sees your reply. Moodius: the boiler.
Be honest. Which list is longer? A  things you know you should do / B  things you actually do Reply A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
A, for nearly everyone. Knowing and doing are different muscles. Most of us train only one.
